name: AutoSubSync
description: Automatically synchronizes external and embedded subtitles across your library, aligning each one against the audio of the media it belongs to. The sync engine is downloaded once on first use and verified against a checksum built into the plugin.
overview: Automatically synchronizes external and embedded subtitles across your library.

versions.changelog: The status panel counts rejected subtitles separately from failed ones, so the pipeline table no longer reports a rejection by the audio check as a synchronization failure. Failure reasons no longer show raw output from the sync engine or the OCR tool, and reason lines no longer repeat the heading they are listed under. A subtitle the engine rescaled past the framerate limit is reported as a failure rather than a rejection, and the audio check setting now says which rejections unticking it will release.

The status panel no longer counts subtitles that are gone from your library, and a subtitle removed as a duplicate stops counting in the same run rather than on the next scan. Retry failed subtitles now starts a full library sync as well. Adds a setting, Run the OCR when a text subtitle of the same language exists, and embedded tracks that an external subtitle already covers are now skipped by default; turn on Process embedded tracks when an external subtitle of the same language exists to keep converting them. Deduplication keeps the unnumbered filename when it picks which copy survives, a .sub with no .idx beside it now says why it cannot be read, and subtitles the engine moved less than the minimum are no longer counted as audio check failures.

A VobSub track holding several languages is now read as one subtitle per language instead of one file containing all of them. OCR output the reader could not resolve is refused rather than written to your library, and image subtitles are read with the right OCR model, including per-script Chinese and Serbian. The status panel now separates a refusal by the audio check from a tool failure, and adds cards for tracks whose source file has gone and tracks not yet run. More titles can be measured by the audio check instead of being left unjudged.

A sync the audio check cannot confirm is no longer written to your library. 1.2.5.0 could stretch a correctly timed subtitle when the audio check reached no verdict and the sync engine reported a small framerate correction; if any of your subtitles are wrong, Roll back everything restores your originals. A new setting, Only sync when audio check is conclusive, is on by default and refuses anything the audio cannot vouch for. The sync engine must now score an alignment of 40 a second, up from 20, and a stretch the audio check never measured is refused. Adds a Retry failed subtitles button under Actions, and stopping the scheduled task now stops syncs started by any other route.

The audio check no longer refuses subtitles it could not actually measure. A sync the engine finished is now kept even when the engine crashes reporting the result, and a subtitle the audio check cannot measure is refused only if the sync engine found no alignment either. Audio check refusals are grouped into readable rows in the log.

Every subtitle is now scored against the video's own audio, before and after syncing. A subtitle the audio already agrees with is left alone and never handed to the engine, and a result the audio disagrees with is discarded instead of written to your library. Results produced before 1.2.4.0 were never checked against the audio; if any of them are wrong, Roll back everything restores your originals. Maximum offset and Minimum offset are gone, automatic sync on new media and refresh after sync now default to off, and the status panel separates subtitles refused by the audio check from failures.
